He previously played for the [[Boston Celtics]] and [[Charlotte Hornets]]. Rozier played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]] before being selected with the 16th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the Celtics. Rozier spent his first four seasons as a reserve with the Celtics until being traded to the Hornets in a [[sign-and-trade deal]]. Rozier was a starter for the Hornets for four-and-a-half seasons before being traded to the Heat. In October 2025, Rozier was arrested by the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] (FBI) for his alleged involvement in [[NBA illegal gambling prosecution|an illegal gambling scheme]]. ==Early life== Rozier was born in [[Youngstown, Ohio]], on March 17, 1994. His father, Terry Rozier Sr., was sent to prison for eight years when Rozier Jr. was two months old.{{cite web |last1=Gardner |first1=David |title=Terry Rozier hopes to carry Louisville, and his family, to new heights |url=https://www.si.com/college/2015/03/02/terry-rozier-louisville-cardinals-acc |website=si.com |access-date=March 7, 2019 |date=March 2, 2015}} In 2005, shortly after Rozier Sr. was released from prison, Rozier Jr. spent a few months with his father before his father was arrested again on charges of involuntary manslaughter for his involvement in a robbery and kidnapping from 2003 that had led to the accidental death of an accomplice.{{Cite news|url=http://www.vindy.com/news/2003/aug/03/youngstown-3-indicted-in-slaying-of-robbery/?print|title=3 indicted in slaying of robbery accomplice|last=Jackson|first=Bob|date=August 3, 2003|work=The Vindicator|access-date=April 18, 2020|archive-date=July 4, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190704112403/http://www.vindy.com/news/2003/aug/03/youngstown-3-indicted-in-slaying-of-robbery/?print|url-status=dead}} Rozier Sr. was then sentenced to 13 years in prison. As a result, Rozier was raised primarily by his mother, Gina Tucker, and his grandmother, Amanda Tucker,{{Cite news|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2015/10/17/terry-rozier-long-outside-shot/ZUT39O5obcrdFC4aAAZjEP/story.html|title=Terry Rozier's long outside shot - The Boston Globe|work=BostonGlobe.com|access-date=May 1, 2018}}{{cite news |last1=Greer |first1=Jeff |title=Louisville's Terry Rozier owes a lot to two women in his life |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2014/02/28/louisvilles-terry-rozier-owes-a-lot-to-two-women-in-his-life/5849345/ |access-date=March 7, 2019 |newspaper=Courier-Journal |date=February 27, 2014}} alongside his brother and half-sister. ==High school career== Rozier starred at [[Shaker Heights High School]] in [[Shaker Heights, Ohio]], graduating in 2012. In his senior year, Rozier averaged 25.6 points, 6.5 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 4.7 steals per game while leading Shaker to a 21–3 record and taking them to the regional semifinals as a senior for the first time since 2002. He was named an All-[[Lake Erie League]] selection for three years and was 74th in recruiting ranking on [[ESPNU]]'s Top 100 Players list in 2012.{{cite web |last1=Jankowsky |first1=Alexa |last2=McMillan |first2=Sean |name-list-style=and |date=April 5, 2015 |title=Former Shaker Guard Declares for the NBA Draft |url=http://shakerite.com/raiderzone/2015/04/05/former-shaker-guard-declares-for-the-nba-draft/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150413042230/http://shakerite.com/raiderzone/2015/04/05/former-shaker-guard-declares-for-the-nba-draft/ |archive-date=April 13, 2015 |access-date=April 6, 2015 |work=The Shakerite}} As Rozier had to improve his grades, Rozier initially played at [[Hargrave Military Academy]] before joining Louisville.{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Alex |date=September 19, 2012 |title=Rozier's Cardinal Career on Hold for Now |url=https://shakerite.com/raiderzone/roziers-cardinal-career-on-hold-for-now/19/2012/ |access-date=November 17, 2024 |work=The Shakerite}} In his 2012–13 campaign at Hargrave, Rozier averaged 29.3 points, 7.8 rebounds and 5.6 assists while the team went 38–8; he also earned the 2012 [[Kentucky Derby Festival Basketball Classic]] MVP and placed second in the dunk and three-point contest that season.{{cite news|last1=tdstout|title=Rozier wins MVP, Chicken wins hearts at Derby Festival Classic|url=https://www.cardchronicle.com/2012/4/7/2932349/rozier-wins-mvp-chicken-wins-hearts-at-derby-festival-classic|access-date=May 19, 2018|work=Card Chronicle|publisher=SB Nation|date=April 7, 2012}} ==College career== As a freshman at [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] in 2013–14, Rozier averaged 7.0 points and 3.1 rebounds per game in 37 games and made the [[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] All-Rookie Team. As a sophomore in 2014–15, Rozier led the Cardinals in scoring with 17.1 points per game and was named second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]].{{cite web|title=Terry Rozier Bio|url=http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/terry_rozier_862096.html|website=GoCards.com|access-date=March 29, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150327061324/http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/terry_rozier_862096.html|archive-date=March 27, 2015}}{{cite web|title=Terry Rozier Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/terry-rozier-1.html|website=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=July 29, 2015}} On March 30, 2015, Rozier and Louisville teammate [[Montrezl Harrell]] declared for the [[2015 NBA draft]].{{cite news |date=March 31, 2015 |others=Contributed by The Associated Press |title=Harrell, Rozier leaving Louisville |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2015/story/_/id/12589253 |access-date=June 27, 2024 |work=ESPN}} ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2015–2019)=== On June 25, 2015, Rozier was selected by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the 16th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].{{cite web |date=June 26, 2015 |title=Celtics Select Rozier, Hunter, Mickey and Thornton in 2015 Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-select-rozier-hunter-mickey-and-thornton-2015-draft |access-date=June 27, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} On July 27, 2015, he signed his rookie-scale contract with the Celtics.{{cite web |date=July 27, 2015 |title=Celtics Sign 2015 First Round Draft Picks Terry Rozier and R.J. Hunter |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-2015-first-round-draft-picks-terry-rozier-and-r.j.-hunter |access-date=June 27, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} During his rookie season, Rozier received multiple assignments to the [[Maine Red Claws]], Boston's [[D-League]] affiliate.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2015-16 NBA Assignments |work=NBA.com |access-date=November 22, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906020056/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |archive-date=September 6, 2015 }} He appeared in 39 regular season games for the Celtics in [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16]], scoring a season-high seven points twice. In his first playoff game, Rozier scored 10 points on 4-of-7 shooting against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |title=Terry Rozier 2015-16 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/roziete01/gamelog/2016 |access-date=October 27, 2016 |work=Basketball-Reference.com}}[[File:Terry Rozier G6 2017 Playoffs.jpg|thumb|right|Rozier in 2017|314x314px]] On November 12, 2016, Rozier scored a career-high 11 points in a 105–99 victory over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899580|title=Isaiah Thomas scores 23 to lead Celtics past Pacers, 105-99|work=ESPN.com|date=November 12, 2016|access-date=November 13, 2016}} He topped that mark nine days later, scoring 12 points in a 99–93 victory over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899655|title=Celtics rally from 13 down in 4th to beat Timberwolves 99-93|work=ESPN.com|date=November 21, 2016|access-date=November 22, 2016}} On December 7, Rozier scored a career-high 16 points in a 117–87 victory over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899764|title=Bradley, Celtics roll to 117-87 victory over Magic|work=ESPN.com|date=December 7, 2016|access-date=December 8, 2016}} On March 19, 2017, he recorded his first career [[double-double]] with 14 points and 10 rebounds in a 105–99 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |title=Terry Rozier 2016-17 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/roziete01/gamelog/2017 |access-date=April 21, 2017 |work=Basketball-Reference.com}} On November 24, 2017, Rozier scored a career-high 23 points in a 118–103 victory over the Orlando Magic.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975020|title=Celtics cruise to 118-103 victory over Magic|work=ESPN.com|date=November 24, 2017|access-date=November 25, 2017}} On December 18, he made a steal and go-ahead dunk with 1.5 seconds remaining that gave the Celtics a narrow 112–111 victory over the Indiana Pacers.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975193|title=Rozier's dunk caps Celtics' rally to 112-111 win over Pacers|work=ESPN.com|date=December 18, 2017|access-date=December 19, 2017}} On January 31, Rozier logged his first career [[triple-double]] in his first NBA start to help the Celtics to a 103–73 victory over the [[New York Knicks]], recording 17 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists while becoming just the second player in NBA history with a triple-double in his first start, joining [[Tony Wroten]], who set the initial record on November 13, 2013, with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975504|title=Rozier's triple-double helps Celtics rout Knicks 103-73|work=ESPN.com|date=January 31, 2018|access-date=January 31, 2018}} Two days later, in his second career start, Rozier scored a career-high 31 points in a 119–110 win over the Hawks.{{cite web|last=Mullen|first=Logan|url=https://nesn.com/2018/02/celtics-wrap-terry-rozier-drops-career-high-31-points-cs-beat-hawks-119-110/|title=Celtics Wrap: Terry Rozier Drops Career-High 31 Points, C's Beat Hawks 119-110|work=nesn.com|date=February 2, 2018|access-date=February 2, 2018}} On March 25, in his sixth start in place of the injured [[Kyrie Irving]], Rozier scored a career-high 33 points in a 104–93 victory over the [[Sacramento Kings]]. He also had five rebounds and three assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975845|title=Rozier scores 33 as Celtics roll past Kings, 104-93|work=ESPN.com|date=March 25, 2018|access-date=March 26, 2018}} In Game 2 of the Celtics' first-round playoff series against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Rozier scored 23 points in helping Boston take a 2–0 series lead with a 120–106 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401029430|title=Brown scores 30, Celtics roll to 120-106 win over Bucks|work=ESPN.com|date=April 17, 2018|access-date=April 17, 2018}} In Game 7, Rozier scored 26 points in a 112–96 victory over the Bucks.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401029437|title=Celtics beat Bucks 112-96 in Game 7, advance to play 76ers|work=ESPN.com|date=April 28, 2018|access-date=April 28, 2018}} In Game 1 of their second-round series against the 76ers, Rozier recorded 29 points, eight rebounds and six assists in a 117–101 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401031671|title=Rozier (29 pts), Tatum (28) help Celtics beat 76ers 117-101|work=ESPN.com|date=April 30, 2018|access-date=April 30, 2018}} In Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Finals, Rozier scored 28 points in a 109–99 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401032845|title=Boston bound: LeBron James pushes Cavs to Game 7 vs. Celtics|work=ESPN.com|date=May 25, 2018|access-date=May 26, 2018}} The Celtics went on to lose in seven games.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401032846|title=LeBron's 35 help Cavs beat Celtics 87-79, reach NBA Finals|work=ESPN.com|date=May 27, 2018|access-date=May 28, 2018}} On November 9, 2018, Rozier scored a then-season-high 22 points in a 123–115 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]], making his first start of the season in place of Irving.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070853|title=Joe Ingles scores 27 points, Jazz outlast Celtics 123-115|work=ESPN.com|date=November 9, 2018|access-date=November 10, 2018}} On January 30, Rozier had 17 points and tied a career high with 10 assists in a 126–94 victory over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web |date=January 30, 2019 |title=Brown, Tatum carry Celtics over Hornets without Irving |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071429 |access-date=January 30, 2019 |work=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2019–2024)=== On July 6, 2019, Rozier was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] as part of a sign-and-trade deal involving [[Kemba Walker]].{{cite web |last=Rochinski |first=Matt |date=July 6, 2019 |title=Charlotte Hornets Acquire Terry Rozier From Boston Celtics In Sign-And-Trade Deal For Kemba Walker |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/charlotte-hornets-acquire-terry-rozier-boston-celtics-sign-and-trade-deal-kemba-walker |work=NBA.com}} As part of the deal, Rozier received a new three-year, $56.7 million contract.{{Cite web|url=https://www.spotrac.com/nba/charlotte-hornets/terry-rozier-17844/|title = Terry Rozier}} On December 18, 2019, Rozier scored a then-career-high 35 points in a 100–98 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite news |last=Bonnell |first=Rick |date=December 18, 2019 |title=Terry Rozier has a career-high 35 points, but Hornets lose to the Cavaliers |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/charlotte-hornets/article238526888.html |access-date=January 25, 2024 |work=Charlotte Observer}} He would surpass that on March 8, 2020, scoring 40 points in a 143–138 double-overtime loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite magazine |last=Northam |first=Mitchell |date=2020-03-09 |title=Terry Rozier drops 40 points, but Charlotte Hornets fall to Atlanta Hawks in 2OT |url=https://www.si.com/nba/hornets/news/terry-rozier-40-nba-hornets-hawks-recap-2020-charlotte |access-date=2024-01-25 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}} The contract the Hornets gave to Rozier at that time was criticized following a poor performance in the 2019 playoffs and losing their longtime star [[Kemba Walker]].{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2019/06/30/terry-rozier-hornets-contract-free-agency-celtics-kemba-walker|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=June 30, 2019|access-date=May 25, Celtics|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220702171112/https://www.si.com/nba/2019/06/30/terry-rozier-hornets-contract-free-agency-celtics-kemba-walker|archive-date=July 2, 2022|url-status=live}} Rozier's performance improved throughout the rest of the season.{{Cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/season-recap-terry-roziers-career-year-highlighted-leadership-adaptability|title=Season Recap: Terry Rozier's Career Year Highlighted by Leadership, 2022|work=[[Charlotte Hornets]]|via=[[NBA]]|last=Wash|first=Quinton|url-status=live}} On December 23, 2020, Rozier put up a then-career-high 42 points, along with three rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block, in a 121–114 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/hornets-news-terry-rozier-knocks-down-10-triples-in-career-high-42-point-outing-vs-cavs/|title=Terry Rozier knocks down 10 triples in career-high 42-point outing for [[New Orleans Pelicans]] on May 9, 2021.{{Cite web |last=McGavic |first=Matthew |date=May 10, 2021 |title=Terry Rozier Scores Career-High vs. Pelicans |url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/terry-rozier-career-high-vs-pels |access-date=March 2, 2023 |website=Louisville Report}} The Hornets finished with a 33–39 record and qualified for the newly implemented [[NBA play-in tournament|play-in tournament]]. However, on May 18, the team's season ended with a 144–117 play-in loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]], which Rozier recorded 16 points, eight rebounds and six assists.{{Cite web |last=Marot |first=Michael |date=May 19, 2021 |title=SABONIS LEADS PACERS PAST HORNETS 144-117 IN PLAY-IN ROUND |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0052000111 |access-date=April 2, 2023 |website=NBA}} On August 24, 2021, Rozier signed a four-year, $97 million contract extension with the Hornets.{{cite news |date=September 22, 2021 |title=Hornets, Terry Rozier officially agree to contract extension |url=https://www.nba.com/news/hornets-terry-rozier-agree-to-contract-extension |access-date=June 27, 2024 |work=NBA.com |language=en}}{{cite magazine |last1=Shapiro |first1=Michael |date=August 19, 2021 |title=Report: Hornets Sign Terry Rozier to Four-Year, $97 Million Extension |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2021/08/19/terry-rozier-hornets-contract-extension-four-years-97-million |access-date=June 27, 2024 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}} On December 29, he scored a season-high 35 points, alongside seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks, in a 116–108 victory over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |date=December 29, 2021 |title=HORNETS TAKE CHARGE EARLY, HOLD ON LATE TO BEAT PACERS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100517 |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=NBA}} On February |title=GRIZZLIES HOLD OFF LATE RALLY BY HORNETS TO WIN 5TH STRAIGHT |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100846 |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} The Hornets finished the season with a 43–39 record and qualified for the play-in tournament for the second straight year, but their season ended on April 13, with a 132–103 play-in loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]], despite 21 points, four rebounds and three assists from Rozier.{{Cite web |last=Newberry |first=Paul |date=April 14, 2022 |title=YOUNG, HUNTER LEAD HAWKS TO 132-103 PLAY-IN ROUT OF HORNETS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0052100111 |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=NBA}} On January 6, 2023, Rozier scored a season-high 39 points, alongside two rebounds and four assists, in a 138–109 victory over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |last=Hoehn |first=Jim |date=January 7, 2023 |title=ROZIER, RECORD 1ST QUARTER LEAD HORNETS PAST BUCKS 138-109 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200583 |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} On January 21, he recorded 34 points, three rebounds, five assists and four steals in a 122–118 victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |last=Henry |first=George |date=January 21, 2023 |title=ROZIER CAPS 19-POINT RALLY, HORNETS END HAWKS' 5-GAME STREAK |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200694 |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=NBA}} ===Miami Heat (2024–2026)=== On January 23, 2024, Rozier was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in exchange for [[Kyle Lowry]] and a protected first-round draft pick.{{cite web|title=HEAT ACQUIRE TERRY ROZIER|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-terry-rozier|website=NBA.com|date=January 23, 2024|access-date=January 23, 2024}} The next day, Rozier made his Heat debut, putting up nine points, five assists, four rebounds, and two steals in a 105–96 loss to the [[2023–24 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/heat-news-terry-rozier-gets-brutally-honest-about-underwhelming-miami-debut-in-loss-to-grizzlies|title=Heat's Terry Rozier gets brutally honest about underwhelming season|2023–24 season]], averaging 16.4 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 4.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Terry Rozier 2023-24 Stats per during the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], recording averages of 10.6 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 2.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Terry Rozier 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3074752/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=July 15, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Rozier was placed on indefinite unpaid leave by the NBA in October 2025 and ordered to stay away from the Heat, one game into the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], pending resolution of an FBI case against Rozier related to sports gambling fraud.{{cite web |last1=Kalland |first1=Robby |title=Terry Rozier arrest: NBPA challenging NBA's suspension without pay for Heat guard amid gambling investigation |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/terry-rozier-arrest-nba-suspension-nbpa-challenge-federal-gambling-investigation/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=1 January 2026}} On April 10, 2026, Rozier gambling prosecution}} On January 30, 2025, the NBA announced that Rozier was under investigation by federal authorities in connection with a sports betting scandal over a 2023 game, when he was with the [[Charlotte Hornets]], where a high volume of bets were placed on the under for Rozier's performance, in which Rozier left the game with a foot injury after nine minutes.{{cite news |last1=Madani |first1=Doha |title=Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier under investigation in federal sports betting probe |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/sports/nba/terry-rozier-betting-investigation-rcna190040 |access-date=30 January 2025 |work=NBC News |date=30 January 2025 |language=en}} Unlike the situation with [[Jontay Porter]] (which led to Porter not playing any more games for the rest of the season before being permanently banned from the NBA), the NBA did allow Rozier to continue playing with the [[Miami Heat]], since Rozier was not charged with any crimes or personally accused of any wrongdoing at the time. On October 23, 2025, Rozier was arrested along with [[Portland Trail Blazers]] head coach [[Chauncey Billups]] and former NBA player [[Damon Jones]] in connection to a much wider federal investigation into [[2025 NBA illegal gambling prosecution|sports betting and gambling]] by various criminal organizations including the [[Bonanno crime family|Bonanno]], [[Gambino crime family|Gambino]], [[Genovese crime family|Genovese]] and [[Lucchese crime family|Lucchese]] crime families of the [[American Mafia]].{{Cite web |last=Clemente |first=Alberto |date=2025-10-23 |title=NBA chaos as FBI arrests Chauncey Billups, Terry Rozier, Damon Jones... |url=https://en.as.com/nba/nba-chaos-as-fbi-arrests-two-big-names-f202510-n/ |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=AS USA |language=en-us}}{{Cite web |last=Morik |first=Ryan |last2=Gaydos |first2=Ryan |date=2025-10-23 |title=NBA legend Chauncey Billups, Heat's Terry Rozier arrested as part of FBI gambling probe |url=https://www.fox4news.com/news/heats-terry-rozier-arrested-part-fbi-sports-betting-probe |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=FOX 35 Orlando |language=en-US}} On December 8, Rozier pled not guilty to federal charges of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and money laundering.{{cite web |last1=Vorkunov |first1=Mike |title=Heat's Terry Rozier pleads not guilty to gambling charges;
